title: The Final Days of Paramahansa Yogananda - A Talk by Sri Daya Mata

# The Final Days of Paramahansa Yogananda

### A Sacred Reminiscence by Sri Daya Mata
*Third President of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India*

In this deeply moving discourse, Sri Daya Mata shares her personal, eyewitness account of the final days and the mahasamadhi (a yogi's final conscious exit from the body) of her beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda. With the characteristic tenderness, devotion, and profound spiritual depth that defined her decades of spiritual leadership, she invites us into those final, sacred weeks of early 1952. Through her words, we are given a window into the mystery of a fully liberated master who, having completed His earthly mission, prepared to merge His consciousness back into the Infinite Spirit.

### The Gathering Shadows of a Divine Departure

In the weeks leading up to March 7, 1952, those of us who lived closest to Paramahansa Yogananda began to sense a subtle, poignant shift in His consciousness. Our beloved Gurudeva was withdrawing. It was not a withdrawal of love—for His love seemed to grow more vast and encompassing with each passing hour—but rather a quiet untying of the final threads that bound His great soul to the physical form. He spent hours in deep, unbroken communion with the Divine Mother, often emerging from His room with eyes that seemed to look right through the physical world into the heart of the Cosmic Delusion.

During this period, Master spoke frequently of His departure. With absolute simplicity and without a trace of fear, He prepared our hearts for the time when His physical presence would no longer be there to guide us. He reminded us that His work on earth was finished, and that the teachings He had brought from the Great Ones would henceforth be the guru.

> "My body will pass, but my work will go on. And my spirit will live in your hearts. When I am gone, only love can take my place. Be absorbed night and day in the love of God, and give that love to all."

We listened with heavy hearts, unable to fully comprehend the magnitude of what He was saying. Yet, in His presence, there was no room for grief. The sheer power of His joy, His humor, and His boundless compassion lifted us above the sorrow of impending separation. He was teaching us, even then, that the relationship between Guru and disciple is not bound by the physical body, but is an eternal bond of the soul.

### The Final Banquet at the Biltmore Hotel

On the evening of March 7, 1952, a banquet was held at the Biltmore Hotel in Los Angeles in honor of the Ambassador of India, His Excellency Binay Ranjan Sen. Gurudeva was scheduled to speak. Sri Daya Mata recalls how, as He prepared to leave the Mt. Washington Mother Center for the banquet, He stopped and looked around His beloved ashram with a deep, silent gaze. It was a silent farewell to the home He had established to spread the sacred science of Kriya Yoga to the world.

At the banquet, Master sat at the speaker's table, radiating an extraordinary aura of peace and divine majesty. When He rose to speak, His voice was filled with a resonant power that thrilled the hearts of everyone in the room. He spoke of the spiritual unity between East and West, of the great heritage of India, and of the ultimate destiny of all souls to find their home in the Infinite.

As He neared the conclusion of His address, He read His beautiful poem, "My India." His voice grew softer, yet it carried an indescribable sweetness and authority:

> "Where Ganges, woods, Himalayan caves, and men dream God—I am hallowed; my body touched that sod."

With these final words, He lifted His eyes to the spiritual eye, and His physical form quietly collapsed to the floor. The great Guru had entered mahasamadhi. He had exited His body as He had lived—in perfect control, completely absorbed in the love of His Divine Mother, at the very moment He spoke of His beloved motherland.

### The Miracle of Incorruptibility

Following His transition, a phenomenon occurred that stunned the scientific and medical world. For twenty-one days after His passing, the physical body of Paramahansa Yogananda remained completely free from decay or disintegration. The director of the Forest Lawn Memorial-Park, where Master's body was placed, wrote in an official notarized letter:

> "No physical decay was visible in his body even twenty days after death... This state of perfect preservation of a body is, so far as we know from mortuary annals, an unparalleled one... Yogananda's body was apparently in a phenomenal state of immutability."

This divine sign was a final, silent sermon from the Master, proving the power of yoga over the laws of matter. For those who loved Him, however, the greatest miracle was not the preservation of His physical body, but the overwhelming presence of His spirit, which became even more tangible after He left His physical temple.

### Moving from the Physical to the Spiritual Presence

Sri Daya Mata describes the immense grief that initially threatened to overwhelm the disciples, and how she found solace through direct communion with the Guru's spirit. She realized that as long as we seek the Guru in the physical form, we limit His omnipresence. It is only when we close our eyes in deep meditation and call to Him in the silence of our hearts that we realize He is closer to us than ever before.

Through her own dark night of sorrow, she heard the sweet voice of the Master speaking within her soul, assuring her that He had not left them, but had only stepped behind the screen of the physical senses. This realization transformed her grief into an unshakeable, ecstatic joy, a joy that she carried throughout her decades of service as the spiritual leader of Self-Realization Fellowship.

### Spiritual Habits for Deepening Attunement with the Guru

To experience the living presence of the Guru and to remain steadfast on the spiritual path, Sri Daya Mata encourages us to cultivate the following daily habits:

* **Practice Deep Meditation Daily:** Dedicate time every morning and evening to practice the Kriya Yoga techniques with deep devotion. It is in the silence of deep meditation that we hear the whisper of the Guru.
* **Develop an Inner Dialogue:** Talk to the Guru throughout the day. Share your joys, your sorrows, your struggles, and your victories with Him. Treat Him as your nearest and dearest friend.
* **Live by His Teachings:** The greatest way to show our love for the Guru is to live according to His ideal. Practice truthfulness, humility, unconditional love, and self-discipline in your daily life.
* **Seek the Divine Mother:** Master's life was entirely dedicated to the Divine Mother. Seek Her with the same childlike simplicity and burning devotion that He demonstrated throughout His life.
* **Meditate on His Eyes:** When the mind is restless, gaze into the eyes of the Guru in His photograph. His eyes are windows to the Infinite and can instantly quiet the storms of the heart.

### A Closing Prayer and Blessing

Let us close our eyes for a moment and feel the sacred, sweet presence of Gurudeva Paramahansa Yogananda wrapping around our souls like a warm blanket of divine love. 

*O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Friend, and Beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda! We bow to Thee. Teach us to love Thee as Thou lovest us. Lift the veil of delusion from our eyes, that we may behold Thy living presence in our hearts and in all creation. Guide our footsteps on the path of Kriya Yoga, and lead us from the darkness of ignorance into the eternal light of Thy love. May Thy blessings be upon us always, and may we ever remain anchored in the fortress of Thy peace.*

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
